newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on exports, cattle data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on exports, cattle data.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish input from export data and from the number of cattle in commercial feedlots in the U.S., traders said.
"The export numbers this morning were good for corn and the cattle numbers were supportive. Also farmers just don't want to sell," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

USDA said there were 8.544 million head of cattle on feed as of November 1, up one percent from a year ago. Pre-report expectations were for a 1/2 percent drop. Also the number of cattle placed on feed during November were at 2.531 million, up 11 percent from a year ago.
USDA early Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export the week ended November 21 totaled 55.563 million bushels, above expectations for 39 million to 50 million bushels.

Corn also found bullish flags from key technical indicators such as the four- and 20-day moving averages. First resistance in December was at $2.73 and second at $2.75-1/2. The session high for December was $2.77-1/2. First support was at $2.71.
Corn closed 1/4 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 2-1/4 at $2.74-3/4.

Key players were Refco Inc with 5.5 million bushels bought in March and two million in December, traders said. Cargill Inc and ADM Investor Services each bought three million bushels of March, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 65,000 contracts, above the 54,992 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Term Commodities bought 1,000 May $2.70 puts at 7-1/4 cents and Dean Witter Reynolds bought 600 March $2.70 calls at 11-3/4 to 12 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, above the 13,173 traded Friday.
